I am interested in developing more theorems around elliptic functions (starting with https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Elliptic/Weierstrass.html). I'd like to know its current status: is it already being worked on, or is it reasonable for me to try working on it?

Let me start with asking about a basic theorem that I find missing: every elliptic function is a rational combination of ℘ and ℘'. What would be the best way to state "rational combination"? On the paper, this is often thought in the field of meromorphic functions, but meromorphic functions in Mathlib, as far as I know, is a bit awkward due to junk values at poles. Is Mathlib's infrastructure ready to state this theorem, or something around meromorphic functions need to be developed first?

Weiyi Wang said:

What would be the best way to state "rational combination"?

Maybe ∈ Set.range (Finsupp.linearCombination ℚ ![℘, ℘']) if you want to be fancy, but probably a simple ∃ a b : ℚ, ... is best.
(idk the maths here; I'm assuming "rational combination" means a linear combination with rationals but maybe not)
It is not just linear combination with rationals. 1/℘ is also valid

Snir Broshi said:

(idk the maths here; I'm assuming "rational combination" means a linear combination with rationals but maybe not)

I'm guessing it means the subfield generated by the ℘ and ℘' and ℂ
Yeah, equivalent way to write this is that the field of elliptic functions = ℂ(℘, ℘')

But I don't think the LHS "field of elliptic functions" (= subfield of meromorphic functions with double period) is statable yet, as we don't have field of meromorhic functions yet (?). To develop that one needs to work with docs#MeromorphicNFAt and patch all the junk values.
So I guess my question is, should this wait for the full development of field of meromorphic functions, or is there a elementary statement we can go for first?

Aaron Liu said:

I'm guessing it means the subfield generated by the ℘ and ℘' and ℂ

So maybe ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin (F := ℂ) {℘, ℘'}? (docs#IntermediateField.adjoin)
An intermediate (sub)field of what big field? That's the question.
I don't think we have the field of meromorphic functions (docs#Meromorphic functions modulo docs#Filter.EventuallyEq on docs#Filter.codiscrete) in mathlib yet

Note that things are delicate here: if a meromorphic function has junk values at its poles then things like sum of meromorphic functions cannot be computed naively: if e.g. (1/z) has junk value 0 at z=0 and ((z-1)/z) also has junk value zero at z=0 (and these are the values which Lean would assign to them) then their sum will have junk value 0 at 0, but their sum should be the constant function 1. As Aaron says we need need to carefully consider equivalence classes, this is the real problem here. Note that Weierstrass P and its derivative both have poles at 0 so this is not just a theoretical problem.
Indeed. Is the recommendation to develop the field of meromorphic functions and handle this part first? Is this being actively worked on?

and (this is going a bit offtopic) if one makes a field of meromorphic functions, should the element be

  • from quotient of MeromorhicOn functions by relation =ᶠ[codiscreteWithin U], or
  • MeromorphicNFOn functions with redefined arithmetic, e.g. f + g is not naive pointwise addition around the pole

Weiyi Wang said:

  • MeromorphicNFOn functions with redefined arithmetic, e.g. f + g is not naive pointwise addition around the pole

Maybe for a meromorphic function f, its evaluation at x is not simply f.toFun x, but the limit of f.toFun y as y tends to x. Since outside the poles f.toFun is continuous, it gives the correct result (even correct for your above f + g, since if the pole cancels out, the limit gives correct answer). If x is a pole of f, then it should give junk value zero (?).
Pinging @Stefan Kebekus on this; I assume he has thought about meromorphic functions a bit.
(I changed the title since the topic has changed)
Perhaps we need to get the rational maps of schemes machinery up and running.
I am unfamiliar with schemes. Could you explain it more?

I'm not sure schemes will answer the original question. We can already make the docs#EllipticCurve associated to a lattice and we have the rational functions on it but by definition it's the field of fractions of C[℘,℘′].\mathbb{C}[\wp,\wp'].C[℘,℘′]. Note that elliptic curves aren't schemes but someone was working on rational maps recently and the issue would be the same. This question is in the analytic category so probably has to be dealt with separately.

if one makes a field of meromorphic functions, should the element be
- ...
- MeromorphicNFOn functions with redefined arithmetic, e.g. f + g is not naive pointwise addition around the pole

After reading more code I realized that the normal form is possibly not unique / not canonical if the set U s not Preperfect, so this doesn't work for the general case
meromorphicity doesn't seem well behaved at isolated points
I guess one option is to declare the normal form to be zero at isolated points?

I got my hand dirty with the quotient approach and now I have a Field (MeromorphicOn f U quotient by =ᶠ[Filter.codiscreteWithin U]) for (h1 : ¬ IsDiscrete U) (h1 : U.Nontrivial) (h2 : IsPreconnected U) (Thanks Aristotle for identifying the needed condition). That was a fun exercise and I'll play with it more to see what might be PR-able

One more (unfortunately unsuccessful) idea is to supplement the definition of a meromorphic function by explicitly including its principal (singular) parts at the singular points. Such definition is good for addition/subtraction, multiplication (require regular parts of Laurent series at singular points), and for contour integration around singular points. But it is bad for division: for example, even the definition of 1/f in terms of meromorphic f will need the locations of zeros and the regular parts of f at these locations. Meromorphic functions like 1/P(f), where P is a polynomial, look terrible within such a defintion.
@Weiyi Wang Is U a subset of the complex line here?
It is a subset of 𝕜 where NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜

I posted #39826 as draft to show what I have got for the field of meromorphic functions. I am open to discussion whether this is the right approach. Meanwhile, I am going to split out small PRs for useful lemmas

Dear all, as @Michael Stoll pointed out, I thought about a solution and discussed it on several occasions with the community. Please give me a little time to come back to you, because we have a small semester break here in Germany, and I am currently on vacation.
No problem! For now I am just having fun experimenting with things. Looking forward to further discussion

Aside from the meromorphic function equivalent class problem, I think another key missing ingredient is the residue theorem. The classic result of elliptic function is "sum of residue" and "sum of meromorphic order" within a fundamental parallelogram is zero, and on paper this is an instant result by taking the contour integral on the parallelogram. Does mathlib have enough tool to do contour integral like this? (I see rectangle one and circle one, but not a generic one)

I have a generalised residue theorem for piecewise C1 paths, that was proven by Claude (following this) on the way to the Valence formula for modular forms. This should work for what you want, but its still very much in the clean up stage.
